statement: You are given a string text. In one step you may insert any single character at any position in the string.
Return the smallest number of steps needed to turn text into a palindrome, a string that reads the same forwards and backwards.

examples.explanation: Its longest palindromic subsequence, such as "mam", has length 3. The other 2 letters each need a partner inserted, giving for example "mbdadbm".
The longest palindromic subsequence has length 3 (for example "ete"), so 8 − 3 = 5 characters need partners.
"noon" already reads the same in both directions, so no letter needs to be inserted.

constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters
